items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: They were built for Caruso. They were built even for a lieder singer

ctx.x: Yeah. Fake mikes. We played last year I think it was, we played in the Executive Suites across the road. They were putting people up for cheap or something, so the guy here made a deal with them and stuff, and so we had to do like two or three hour thing, over there, and the loyal fans trooped over to their bar area, their lounge. And the lounge had © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

no piano, it had never had any music. It was just some place where they piped in this stuff, and the big T.V. screens so they could watch the testosterones playing the spiroketes you know, in football or something. And so that was off, and so there we were and they’d forgotten to put a sound system in. It was absolutely acoustic. It was like 1930 when you played a job at a dance hall. There wasn’t anything.
